title: BCOR-rearranged sarcomas: In silico insights into altered domains and BCOR interactions.
authors: Madarasz, Kristof; Motyan, Janos Andras; Chang Chien, Yi-Che; Bedekovics, Judit; Csoma, Szilvia Lilla; Mehes, Gabor; Mokanszki, Attila
one_liner_zh: 该文通过AlphaFold3和PRODIGY等计算手段分析BCOR融合蛋白的结构域改变及与PCGF1的结合亲和力变化，属于蛋白质-蛋白质互作而非TF-DNA体系，但结构预测与结合亲和力计算方法可迁移至TF-DNA互作建模，故给予中档评分。
abstract: BCOR (BCL-6 corepressor) rearranged small round cell sarcoma (BRS) represents an uncommon soft tissue malignancy, frequently characterized by the BCOR::CCNB3 fusion. Other noteworthy fusions include BCOR::MAML3, BCOR::CLGN, BCOR::MAML1, ZC3H7B::BCOR, KMT2D::BCOR, CIITA::BCOR, RTL9::BCOR, and AHR::BCOR. The BCOR gene plays a pivotal role in the Polycomb Repressive Complex 1 (PRC1), essential for histone modification and gene silencing. It interfaces with the Polycomb group RING finger homolog (PCGF1). This study employed comprehensive in silico methodologies to investigate the structural and functional effects of BCOR fusion events in BRS. The analysis revealed significant alterations in the domain architecture of BCOR, which resulted in the loss of BCL6-regulated transcriptional repression. Furthermore, IUPred3 prediction indicated a significant increase in disorder in the C-terminal regions of the BCOR in the fusion proteins. A detailed analysis of the physicochemical properties by ProtParam revealed a decrease in isoelectric point, stability, and hydrophobicity. The analysis of protein structures predicted by AlphaFold3 using the PRODIGY algorithm revealed statistically significant deviations in binding affinities for BCOR-PCGF1 dimers and a non-canonical PRC1 variant tetramer compared to the wild-type BCOR. The findings provide a comprehensive summary and elucidation of the fusion proteome associated with BRS, suggesting a substantial impact on the stability and functionality of the fusion proteins, thereby contributing to the oncogenic mechanisms underlying BRS. In this study, we provide the first compilation and comparative analysis of the known BCOR fusions of BRS and introduce a new in silico approach to enhance a better understanding of the molecular basis of BRS.
abstract_zh: BCOR（BCL-6共抑制因子）重排的小圆细胞肉瘤（BRS）是一种罕见的软组织恶性肿瘤，常以BCOR::CCNB3融合为特征。其他值得注意的融合包括BCOR::MAML3、BCOR::CLGN、BCOR::MAML1、ZC3H7B::BCOR、KMT2D::BCOR、CIITA::BCOR、RTL9::BCOR和AHR::BCOR。BCOR基因在Polycomb抑制复合物1（PRC1）中发挥关键作用，对组蛋白修饰和基因沉默至关重要。它与Polycomb组RING指同源物（PCGF1）相互作用。本研究采用全面的计算机模拟方法，探讨BRS中BCOR融合事件的结构和功能影响。分析揭示了BCOR结构域架构的显著改变，导致BCL6调控的转录抑制功能丧失。此外，IUPred3预测显示，融合蛋白中BCOR的C端区域无序性显著增加。通过ProtParam对理化性质的详细分析显示，等电点、稳定性和疏水性均有所降低。使用AlphaFold3预测的蛋白质结构，并通过PRODIGY算法分析，揭示了与野生型BCOR相比，BCOR-PCGF1二聚体和非经典PRC1变体四聚体的结合亲和力存在统计学显著偏差。这些发现为BRS相关的融合蛋白质组提供了全面的总结和阐释，表明融合蛋白的稳定性和功能受到显著影响，从而促进了BRS的致癌机制。在本研究中，我们首次对BRS已知的BCOR融合进行了汇编和比较分析，并引入了一种新的计算机模拟方法，以增强对BRS分子基础的理解。
